# powerhmc_sys_config (Resource)

Manages configuration of an IBM Power HMC managed system.

A managed system (CEC) is a physical IBM Power server managed by an HMC. Use this
resource to manage system-wide settings such as memory mirroring, memory region
size, power saving mode, and LPAR start policy on an existing managed system.

~> **This resource is import-only.** You must `terraform import` the managed
system before you can apply this resource (Create is unsupported and returns an
error). Deleting the resource only removes it from Terraform state — the physical
system is not affected.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# The powerhmc_sys_config resource manages the configuration of an EXISTING
# managed system (CEC). It cannot create or physically delete a system:
#
#   * You MUST `terraform import` the system before applying (see examples/resources/powerhmc_sys_config/import.sh).
#   * Deleting the resource only removes it from Terraform state.
#
# Some settings only take effect after the next system power-on or restart,
# and requested_huge_pages can only be changed while the system is powered off.

resource "powerhmc_sys_config" "server" {
  name = "existing-server-name" # must match the imported system name

  # requested_huge_pages can only be changed while the system is powered off;
  # a plan that changes it on a running system is rejected.
  requested_huge_pages       = 100
  mem_mirroring_mode         = "system firmware only" # "none" | "system firmware only"
  mem_region_size            = "256"
  power_on_lpar_start_policy = "autostart" # "autorecovery" | "autostart" | "userinit"
  power_off_policy           = false
  power_saving_mode          = "Maximum_Performance"

  # Bound how long Terraform waits for the configuration update to apply.
  timeouts {
    update = "20m"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Name of the managed system as it appears in HMC. Must match the name used during import and can be updated after import.

### Optional

- `mem_mirroring_mode` (String) Memory mirroring mode for the managed system.
Changes to this setting take effect on the next system power-on or system restart.
- `mem_region_size` (String) Indicates the size of the memory blocks that can be assigned to partitions. Any changes that you make will be applied after the next system restart.
- `power_off_policy` (Boolean) Automatically power off system when all LPARs shut down.
- `power_on_lpar_start_policy` (String) Partition start policy controls automatic LPAR startup behavior.
Any changes that you make takes effect after the next system restart.
- `power_saving_mode` (String) Power saving mode for the managed system. Supported values vary by system generation (Power10/Power11). The system will accept any value from SupportedPowerSavingModeTypes.
- `requested_huge_pages` (Number) The number of pages of huge page memory that is requested by the managed system.
You can change this value only when the managed system is powered off.
- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `state` (String) Current state of the managed system.
- `uuid` (String) The UUID of the managed system (computed from HMC after import).

<a id="nestedblock--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `update` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).

## Notes

### Powered-off-only settings

`requested_huge_pages` can only be changed while the managed system is in a
powered-off state. If the system is not powered off, the plan is rejected with a
descriptive error.

### Settings that require a restart

Many settings do not take effect immediately. `mem_mirroring_mode`,
`mem_region_size`, and `power_on_lpar_start_policy` are applied only after the
next system power-on or restart. Plan your maintenance windows accordingly.

### Read-only data source

A `powerhmc_sys_config` data source is also available if you only need to query
the current configuration of a managed system without managing it.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

```shell
# Managed systems are imported by their name as it appears in the HMC.
# Import is REQUIRED before the resource can be applied.
terraform import powerhmc_sys_config.server existing-server-name
```
